previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, GJ tube placement, and prior cecal volvulus presented with a two-day history of diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had elevated white blood cell count on admission but no signs of infection, and blood and urine cultures were negative. CT imaging showed no bowel obstruction or acute abdominal process. Pain was initially managed with IV morphine, but due to concerns about opioid-induced gastric slowing, she was transitioned to tramadol. Nausea was treated with lorazepam and tube feeds were successfully restarted. Her leukocytosis resolved spontaneously. As part of a planned outpatient procedure, her GJ tube was replaced by interventional radiology during the admission. She improved clinically, tolerated full tube feeds, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid opiates, continue new and home medications, and follow up with her primary care provider.

# Abdominal pain: her pain was attributed to a likely 
gastroparesis flare. She had a CT abdomen/pelvis without 
evidence of obstruction or acute pathology. She was initially 
made NPO and tube feeds were resumed via her G-J tube. She did 
have a leukocytosis which seems chronic since the end of ___, 
however an infectious etiology of her abdominal pain was less 
likely as she was non-toxic appearing with normal CT scan.  It 
is unclear if she has adhesions given multiple abdominal 
surgeries in the past as a cause of her abdominal pain as well.  
An IgA, TTG, and CRP were added on the day of discharge and 
returned WNL. She has follow up with a new GI physician at ___. 
She should continue tube feeds until able to tolerate PO. 
Patient has TFs at home and will resume her home regimen of 
morphine ___ prn, lorazepam prn, and zofran prn. 

# Leukocytosis: The patient has had a chronic leukocytosis since 
end ___ with neutrophil predominance. She has been afebrile 
and infectious work has been negative including UA, CXR and CT 
scan. If her leukocytosis persists she may benefit from hem-onc 
referral as an outpatient. 

# Hypertension: The patient's blood pressures were persistently 
elevated on admission and she was started on an 
anti-hypertensive regimen. Lisinopril was increased to 40 mg 
daily on the day of discharge and pressures should be followed 
as an outpatient.

# Hypothyroidism - The patient's TSH elevated at 6.0. Ddx 
includes sick euthyroid vs malabsorption of her Synthroid in the 
setting of multiple GI surgeries. Her levothyroxine dose was not 
changed. Repeat TSH should be done as an outpatient, after her 
acute GI issues resolve. If still elevated levothyroxine should 
be titrated
